title: Affine localization near an arbitrary closed subset
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ any ideal, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $C=V(I)=\{\mathfrak q:I\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$ and $S=\{s\in A:s\bmod I\text{ is a unit in }A/I\}$. Let $B=S^{-1}A$ be the ring of fractions $a/s$ with $a\in A$ and $s\in S$, where $a/s=a\prime/s\prime$ if some $t\in S$ annihilates $as\prime-a\prime s$, and let $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$ be the canonical morphism. Then $h$ is weakly etale [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism] and a homeomorphism onto $\{\mathfrak p:\exists\mathfrak q\supseteq I,\ \mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$, the points of $T$ specializing to $C$. In particular its image contains $C$, and every point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ specializes within $\operatorname{Spec}B$ to a point whose image lies in $C$. No finite-generation hypothesis on $I$ or on the closed subset $C$ is imposed.
